description: Create a one-time mount ticket for a sandbox. The result is the mount session with its ticket (single use, valid for minutes) and mount_command, a convenience hint for a person. Agents must construct the documented mountable mount --ticket-stdin --json command with separately quoted arguments, not evaluate mount_command. Pass the ticket through stdin from MOUNTABLE_TICKET, never in an argument list or log. /mnt/mountable is only a default: use a caller-approved writable directory. Use an existing approved CLI; if installation is authorized, choose npm install --global --ignore-scripts mountable-cli or uv tool install mountable, then mountable version. Report setup blockers instead of using sudo or a remote shell installer. Linux mounts need FUSE. Validate the nonempty ticket and selected filesystem ID, then wait for a mounted JSON event matching the intended path, filesystem and mode before using the directory. Retries: pass your own idempotency_key and reuse it when retrying after an unknown outcome. A replay returns the existing session without a ticket. If that session is still requested, its ticket was lost: this tool revokes it and creates a new one with a fresh key, and the result names the old one as replaced_session_id. If it is active or later, the ticket was used: nothing is revoked and the tool fails with ticket_already_used; use a new idempotency_key for another mount. idempotency_conflict means an identical request is in progress. If the outcome is unknown (network_error or outcome_unknown), the error's idempotency_key is the key that request was sent with: retry with exactly that key, even if you did not choose it. On rate_limited, wait retry_after seconds before retrying.

idempotency_key.description: a key you choose and reuse when retrying this request; a new key for each new mount

max_duration_seconds.description: the session's maximum duration in seconds; optional (default 12 hours, at most the API key's or login's expiry)

name: create_mount_ticket
